questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why violent video games are bad for young children
How to design and sell a successful video game
The growth of professional video gaming as a business
The history of the Olympic Games and new sports
questions.why: Neil says the business of eSports is the topic of the programme.

questions.q: Why does Sam say Neil's gaming with his kids isn't really eSports?
options: eSports are huge events with well-paid professionals
eSports are only played by teenagers in their bedrooms
eSports need special computers that cost thousands
eSports are only ever played online, never in person
questions.why: She says tens of thousands watch, and the players are professional with huge salaries.

questions.q: Which big sports event will include eSports?
options: The 2020 Olympics
The football World Cup
The Commonwealth Games
The 2022 Asian Games
questions.why: Neil says eSports are going to be included in the 2022 Asian Games.

questions.q: What does Gabriël Rau think about the growth of eSports?
options: It is dangerous for young people's health and sleep
It may become as normal as traditional sports
It will soon become less popular than it is today
It should only be for adults over the age of eighteen
questions.why: He says it 'might become as normal as sports are right now'.

questions.q: What disadvantage of video games does Gabriël Rau mention?
options: They are expensive
They are bad for your eyes
They take up a lot of time
They make people aggressive

questions.q: Why does Neil mention playing until the middle of the night?
options: To show he is good enough to be a professional player
To give a personal example of how games eat up time
To complain that his children never go to bed on time
To recommend playing at night when it is quieter
questions.why: He says he knows from experience that many hours can pass while playing.

questions.q: What does Gabriël Rau advise for introducing children to video games?
options: Use discipline, such as strict time limits
Let them play as much as they want
Wait until they are teenagers
Only let them play with friends
questions.why: He says 'discipline is the way to go', and Sam gives the example of a one-hour limit.

questions.q: What is the eSports student's main ambition?
options: To become a famous professional player and win prizes
To design new video games for a big company
To teach eSports courses at a university
To organise events that create experiences for others
questions.why: She wants to put an event together 'not so much to play it'.
